merged.title: fix(launcher): read a repository's mods at its newest release
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Add from a link with `https://github.com/OpenRAC/openrac-mods` offered only xbox-icons for Going Commando. Difficulty, item-randomizer and multiplayer came back as "Not for this game's disc (rac2, ntsc)".

**Why:** `remote::read_github` reads every manifest at `eligible.first()`, the first release in GitHub's list, on the assumption that this is the newest. GitHub doesn't list releases by date. For openrac-mods the first entry was `xbox-icons-v1.1.0` (commit f343f2f, 2026-11-08 04:52 UTC). At that commit the three gameplay mods were still rac1-only: difficulty 1.3.0, item-randomizer 2.0.0 and multiplayer 0.10.0. The newest release is `lock-strafe-v1.1.1`.

**Fix:**
- The eligible releases are sorted newest first, by `created_at` (the release commit's date), falling back to `published_at`, before the manifests are read.
- A native mod whose version at that release has no release of its own yet is now described from its own newest release, the one that would actually be installed, instea

merged.title: fix(hostgen): run the hook call matched C writes as inline assembly
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Hrugis Cloud (Going Commando v1.01) has been broken since #408: the ship never spawns, the HUD never draws, and the camera stays on the hangar.

**Cause.** The rac2-decomp bump in #408 (11876eec → d29456d6) brought in matched C for both moby update loops, `func_002B6658` and `func_L00_0032CF60`. They call each object's update hook through `call_hook` (rac2-decomp `include/common.h`), which is inline asm: `beq %1,$0,1f; move $4,%2; jal $31,%1`. hostgen turned that statement into a barrier, so no update hook ran. Before the bump both loops were translated from their assembly, which makes the call. The report listed it under "Inline assembly the host does not run" (`call_hook | beq, move, jal, 1:`).

**Fix.** An asm statement that calls through a register with a0 set (with or without the null check, `beq`/`beqz`, `jal`/`jalr`, `$4`/`$a0`) is now lowered to that call, through `openrac_guest_call_a0` (guest.h, built on `openrac_guest_call_regs` as asmc.py's jalr is). rac1's moby update loop

merged.title: feat(baker): improve adaptive probe baking and emission
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Default to adaptive 64–512 ray sampling with progressive Sobol directions, separate lighting and visibility convergence, and nearby mesh-light sampling.
- Reuse an Embree HIGH scene between room planning and probe tracing.
- Support texture and mesh emission with per-material cutout control, and migrate the reviewed RAC1 and RAC2 material profiles to area-weighted mesh emission. Provide a migration command for prepared exports.
- Keep Vulkan GPU baking opt-in with a fixed ray budget.

## Validation

- Windows enhanced baker build and targeted native tests, including Vulkan probe sampling, early lighting, and the automatic baker pipeline. The pipeline passed on rerun after a Windows fixture-directory rename error.
- Editor and bake-planning test suites, PAL/NTSC host-hook parity checks, strict changed-line conventions, and dependency layering checks.
- Fresh Aridia bake verified all 188 grids. The cache reused the verified bake on update, and the final adaptive-loop cleanu

merged.title: feat(baker): add mesh emission calculator
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Add `openrac-enhanced-baker --calculate-mesh-emission LEVEL_DIR` to print an override catalog with area-weighted linear `bake_mesh_rgb` per static model and material slot. The command uses the existing migration integrator and reads the original emission inputs even when the export has already been migrated. It leaves the export files untouched.

## Verification

- Built the enhanced baker on Windows and passed `enhanced_baker_cli`, including a regression test with a deliberately different stored RGB value.
- Original and migrated Aridia exports produced identical JSON for 16 material slots. The results matched a fresh migration and differed from the checked-in values by at most 4.83e-9 per channel.
- Changed-line clang-format and layering checks passed locally.

Migrated exports need their original geometry, textures and source emission settings. Local testing used Windows and the Aridia NTSC export.

merged.title: feat(sdk): Going Commando's item equip as a hook point
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando's EquipItem (`func_002AD860`; PAL `func_002AE3C0`, USA v2.00 `func_002AE6C8`) as the hook point `rac2.item.equip`, `i32(i32)`.

Most givers call it right after GiveInventoryItem with the same id: Todano's Sheepinator pickup (`func_L12_00402DF8`), the Tractor Beam, the Thermanator, the Swingshot, the Mapper, the Hypnomatic, the Charge Boots, and the vendor after a purchase. A mod that hooks `rac2.item.give` to hand out something else (the item randomizer) had no way to stop the equip that follows, so the hero ended up holding an item he does not own. That is a player's report: the Sheepinator was in his hand, never in the weapon lists, and gone once put away. The randomizer's side is in openrac-mods.

- `sdk/bindings/rac2.json`, and a hook row in each disc's `libraries.tsv`. The PAL and v2.00 names come from the release views, as `Item_Give`'s do.
- Regenerated with `gen_binding.py` and `gen_reference.py`; `rac2.h` by hand.
- `RAC2_IDENTIFIED.tsv` records EquipItem.
- SDK

merged.title: fix(rac2): the mods' play calls before the mods load
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando installed its tools and its play table (tools.c, play.c) from crt0 (entry.c, func_00131AE8). main.cpp loads the mods before the game runs, and each mod keeps the play table it finds at load (mods.cpp, fill_play_api). So in Going Commando every mod got a null table:

- play_status failed. The item randomizer's per-tick work never ran: the vendor's stock, Endako's own items, and a level start's rewards.
- The multiplayer mod refused to load ("this OpenRAC has no play calls for Going Commando").

The fix is a constructor in entry.c that installs them first, as Ratchet & Clank's boot.c already does. The link keeps entry.c because the entry point is named. crt0 installs them again, which is harmless.

Checked on box2 with the NTSC-U build. Before the fix, the item randomizer's play_status returned -1 at every tick. After it, play_status answers (level 4, phase 2, ...). The PAL and USA v2.00 builds compile and link.

merged.title: fix(port): keep water vertex data in a single fetch
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Fix a stretched triangle in Novalis enhanced water on Radeon Vulkan. The baked water strip and live CPU vertices agreed, but the rendered face picked up mismatched triangle data. Fetch each vertex's barycentric weights and coarse triangle index as one integer attribute and decode the original float bits in the shader.

The fix applies to the shared enhanced-water draw path and works with existing water bakes.

## Verification

- Reproduced and verified the fix at the same Novalis camera position on Windows, RAC1 NTSC-U, Radeon 780M and Vulkan using the same bake.
- Rebuilt and passed the focused `water_mesh`, `water_gpu`, and `effect_material` tests.
- Changed-line clang-format and layering checks passed. clang-tidy reported no diagnostics in the changed source.

The in-game reproduction was verified on NTSC-U. PAL gameplay was not tested locally.

A global with no address used to stub its whole function; it is covered by the same check.

- rac2-ntsc: derived_names.json gives the ref its address (level 0 0x002E6EF8, called thr

merged.title: fix(launcher): check the mod list again when "Check for updates" is pressed
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The Mods tab's "Check for updates" never showed new versions of mods that are in the mod index.

**Why.** The button calls `plugins_check_updates`, the per-repository look. That look drops every mod the index lists (`updates.retain(|u| !listed.contains(&u.id))`), because those are left to `mods_auto_update`. But `mods_auto_update` only runs at launcher start, every 6 hours and before Play, so pressing the button never looked at the index again. A version published after the session's last index fetch stayed hidden until one of those timers or Play ran, and meanwhile the button said "Every mod from a link is up to date". On 2026-11-09 the launcher started at 05:03:07, 16 s after the index went up at 05:02:51 with difficulty 1.5.0, xbox-icons 1.2.0 and item-randomizer 2.3.0. The new versions only showed after the before-Play look at 05:09.

**Fix.**
- `mods_updates` takes `fresh`.
- "Check for updates" first runs `checkIndex`, which fetches the index again. With updates on by themselves

merged.title: feat(launcher): choose Going Commando weapon versions, Mega included
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The Going Commando save editor showed a weapon's version but never let you change it, so there was no way to turn on the challenge-mode Mega versions the way rac1's editor turns on golden weapons. Now there is.

## How the game does it (from the retail code)

- A weapon's version is its record, chunk 30 (`D_00139568`). Records are 0xE0-byte rows of `D_00239BA0`: +0x04 is the version (0..3), +0x4A/+0x4C link the chain, +0x6C is the experience step, +0x8E the full ammo, +0x80 the price.

- **V3, the Mega upgrade**: the vendor's list (`func_002F6608`) offers it only in challenge mode (`func_00288D58`: progress +0x12 non-zero) for an owned weapon on a record with no step left (V2). The purchase (0x002F8F78) gives V3's full ammo, then `func_002887B0` moves the record two rows down and sets experience to 0.
- **V4** is V3's experience step, in cha

merged.title: feat(launcher): allow Going Commando Mega weapon versions outside challenge mode
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The save editor offers V3 and V4 (and the two-row weapons' second version) on every save, not only after challenge mode started. A version is a row of the weapon table, so owning one loads fine; outside challenge mode the game only gates earning them.

A V3 there still earns experience (`func_002A6C58` adds it with no mode test) but never upgrades to V4: the tick `func_L00_002D5EB8` skips the row while `func_00288D58` is 0. The editor says so; V4 can be picked directly. Other rules unchanged (owned weapons, not the one in hand, experience and ammo within the version's range).

Checked on box2 in the port (hidden, no challenge mode): a Chopper at V3 with experience exactly at V4's step stayed V3 800 frames later; a Pulse Rifle set to V4 ran without a crash.

merged.author: nickyyOO

**Before:** a mod's own files (the SDK's `data_dir`, `files/share/openrac/mod-data/<id>`) had no place of their own in the Files app. Mods that worked out their own folder, like the item randomizer, wrote where the player could not reach at all, so its spoiler log could not be opened on Android.

merged.title: fix(port): stop eating pad presses while a notification is shown
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** while a notification card was on screen (the Start+Select hint at start, "Screenshot saved", freecam), the drawer and the desktop menu ran `menu_closed()` every frame, even with the menu already shut. That called `hold_back_held()` each frame, so every held button was held back until let go and taps were dropped. The game saw a press for one window frame at most: many presses were missed (worse at 120 Hz) and holds (run, high jump) did not work. It also reset the Start+Select chord.

**After:** `menu_closed()` runs once, on the frame the menu finishes shutting. Presses and holds reach the game while a card is up.

**How:** `drawer()` and `menu_window()` remember whether the menu was out before the slide and call `menu_closed()` only on that change.

merged.title: feat(launcher): turn Game colours on by default
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Closes #426

**Before:** Game colours (Settings > General) was off by default, so every game wore the launcher's gold.

**After:** Game colours is on by default: each game wears its own bar, gold and coal in the launcher and in the game's menu. Turning it off still gives the gold to every game.

**How:** `gameColors` defaults to true in the core config (a settings file without the key gets it on); the page's fallbacks and the first-paint value kept in localStorage follow (it now keeps "0" when off, so nothing kept means on). STYLE.md and comments updated, Config.ts regenerated. The mock's `?gameColors` flag became `?gold` (colours off).

**Tested:** `cargo test` (config, theme, generated_types), `yarn verify` (typecheck, lint, format, 325 tests). Not tested on a device. A launcher.json saved by a dev build since #393 already holds `"gameColors": false`, so such a launcher stays off until the switch is turned on once.

opened.untrustedBody:
Going Commando installed its tools and its play table (tools.c, play.c) from crt0 (entry.c, func_00131AE8). main.cpp loads the mods before the game runs, and each mod keeps the play table it finds at load (mods.cpp, fill_play_api). So in Going Commando every mod got a null table:

The fix is a constructor in entry.c that installs them first, as Ratchet & Clank's boot.c already does. The link keeps entry.c because the entry point is named. crt0 installs them again, which is harmless.

Checked on box2 with the NTSC-U build. Before the fix, the item randomizer's play_status returned -1 at every tick. After it, play_status answers (level 4, phase 2, ...). The PAL and USA v2.00 builds compile and link.

The Mods tab's "Check for updates" never showed new versions of mods that are in the mod index.

**Before:** while a notification card was on screen (the Start+Select hint at start, "Screenshot saved", freecam), the drawer and the desktop menu ran `menu_closed()` every frame, even with the menu already shut. opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
Matches 298 US functions and 24 PAL functions. US goes from 7,673 to 7,967 functions (12.88% → 14.18% of the code), PAL from 8,044 to 8,103 (14.62% → 14.89%).

## How

Most are **shape twins**: functions whose instructions are those of a function already matched in C, with other constants and addresses (OpenRAC's `tools/mips.py` shape fingerprint over the US and PAL catalogues). For each one, the twin's C was copied and then:

- every constant that differs was set to retail's (from the compiled diff), floats included: the PAL twins of US functions often change 60 Hz values for 50 Hz ones (`60.0f` → `50.0f`, `0.2f` → `0.24f`);
- callees and globals were renamed to what the disc reaches, from the relocations of our object against the retail words (for PAL, the PAL addresses, as `src/pal/` files do);
- comments were dropped, since they described the twin.

Fourteen are mid-size functions decompiled by hand.

**Before:** the item randomizer worked out its own folder (`dev.openrac.launcher/mods/item-randomizer`), and multiplayer wrote `mp-trace.log` to the game's working directory. On Android both are hidden in the app's storage, so the spoiler log, `seed.txt` and the verbose log could not be opened.

**After:** both mods use the folder the port gives them (`data_dir`, interface 1.11): `mod-data/<id>` beside the memory cards. On Android that is OpenRAC > Mod files > <id> in the Files app. The randomizer copies a seed remembered in the old folder once, so a blank seed keeps the same game; old spoiler logs stay where they were. A port without `data_dir` keeps the old places. Archipelago already used `data_dir`; no other mod writes files.

opened.title: fix: keep mods' files in the port's mod folder (item-randomizer 2.4.1, multiplayer 0.12.3)
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the item randomizer worked out its own folder (`dev.openrac.launcher/mods/item-randomizer`), and multiplayer wrote `mp-trace.log` to the game's working directory. On Android both are hidden in the app's storage, so the spoiler log, `seed.txt` and the verbose log could not be opened.

**After:** both mods use the folder the port gives them (`data_dir`, interface 1.11): `mod-data/<id>` beside the memory cards. On Android that is OpenRAC > Mod files > <id> in the Files app. The randomizer copies a seed remembered in the old folder once, so a blank seed keeps the same game; old spoiler logs stay where they were. A port without `data_dir` keeps the old places. Archipelago already used `data_dir`; no other mod writes files.

**How:** item-randomizer: `mod.c` passes `api->data_dir(mod)` to `rando_set_port_dir`; `paths.c` picks `OPENRAC_MOD_DATA_DIR`, then the port's folder, then the old one. Multiplayer: `mod.data_dir()` for `mp-trace.log`, else the working directory. Versions 2.4
